skill: Solve first-order linear initial value problems using integrating factors, selecting an integrating factor and the unique particular solution.
learner_operation: Normalize the ODE, integrate P to identify I, integrate I Q, divide by I, and impose the initial value; distinguish distractors by these dependencies rather than choice layout.
reasoning_steps: Write y prime + P y = Q (divide by x for the nonstandard source).
Compute I = exp(integral P dx); verify I prime = P I.
Rewrite (I y) prime = I Q and integrate.
Use y(x0)=y0 to determine C and select the corresponding solution.
response_contract: Two select fields: field-1 integrating factor (four choices), field-2 particular solution (four or five source choices); not free entry. Canonical example has a worked solution without answer fields.
difficulty: Easy requested. Source has one unlabelled constant-coefficient example, moderate constant/rational/trigonometric examples, and hard linear-P examples. Small constant-coefficient variations are defensible easy practice; preserve other source profiles for replay without asserting all are easy.
invariants: First-order linear ODE and one initial condition on a nonsingular interval.
An integrating factor is nonzero and satisfies I prime=P I.
Correct y satisfies both ODE and initial condition.
Two select fields with unambiguous mathematically distinct choices after correcting captured duplicate choices.
Worked solution follows standardization, integrating factor, product derivative, integration and initial condition.
permitted_variations: Coefficients, signs, initial values and regular initial locations may change with all dependent content recomputed.
Same-method source families: constant forcing; proportional monomial P,Q; power integrating factors with polynomial/trig forcing; exponential cancellation with polynomial or sine forcing.
Correct option positions, choice order, distractor profiles, sign of integration constant, and which expressions satisfy ODE/initial condition are eligible answer-bearing assignments.
Changing initial condition should preserve I but generally change y; changing P generally changes both. Shuffling choices preserves mathematical responses but changes selection IDs/positions.

fixed_features.feature: Two requested quantities I and y
fixed_features.justification: Every banked source explicitly requests these two decisions.
Select response contract; source duplicates are defects, not pedagogical constraints.

source_cases.problem:
Consider the following initial value problem.
$\frac{dy}{dx} + y = 1, y(0) =-3$

Select the correct options below.

An integrating factor for this equation is $I(x) =$ {{field-1}}.

The solution to the initial value problem is $y(x) =$ {{field-2}}.

Consider the following initial value problem.

$$
\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}+\frac{x}{2}\cdot y=x,\,y(0)=1
$$

Select the correct options below.

$\,$ An integrating factor for this equation is $I(x)=$ {{field-1}}.

$\,$ The solution to the initial value problem is $y(x)=$ {{field-2}}.

Consider the following initial value problem.

$$
x\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}+2y=4{x}^{2},\,y(1)=2
$$

Select the correct options below.$\,$ An integrating factor for this equation is $I(x)=$ {{field-1}}.

$\,$ The solution to the initial value problem is $y(x)=$ {{field-2}}.

Consider the following initial value problem.

$$
\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}+\frac{2y}{x}=\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡x}{{x}^{2}},\,y(\pi )=0
$$

Select the correct options below.$\,$ An integrating factor for this equation is $I(x)=$ {{field-1}}.

$\,$ The solution to the initial value problem is $y(x)=$ {{field-2}}.

Consider the following initial value problem.

$$
\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}+\frac{1}{x}y=\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡x}{x},\,x>0,\,y\left(\frac{\pi }{2}\right)=1
$$

Select the correct options below.$\,$ An integrating factor for this equation is $I(x)=$ {{field-1}}.

$\,$ The solution to the initial value problem is $y(x)=$ {{field-2}}.

Consider the following initial value problem.

$$
\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}+y=2x{e}^{-x},\,y(0)=-2
$$

Select the correct options below.$\,$ An integrating factor for this equation is $I(x)=$ {{field-1}}.

$\,$ The solution to the initial value problem is $y(x)=$ {{field-2}}.

Consider the following initial value problem.

$$
\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}+4y=8,\,y(0)=-1
$$

Select the correct options below.$\,$ An integrating factor for this equation is $I(x)=$ {{field-1}}.

$\,$ The solution to the initial value problem is $y(x)=$ {{field-2}}.

Consider the following initial value problem.

$$
\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}+\frac{x}{6}y=x,\,y(0)=5
$$

Select the correct options below.
$\,$ An integrating factor for this equation is $I(x)=$ {{field-1}}.

$\,$ The solution to the initial value problem is $y(x)=$ {{field-2}}.

Consider the following initial value problem.

$$
\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}-2y={e}^{2x}\operatorname{sin}⁡x,\,y(0)=4
$$

Select the correct options below.

$\,$ An integrating factor for this equation is $I(x)=$ {{field-1}}.

$\,$ The solution to the initial value problem is $y(x)=$ {{field-2}}.
